key_insight: SafeDiSTL decomposes shared safety constraint violations in multi-agent RL by using STL robustness sensitivities to assign each cost increment to the agents most responsible, even when effects are delayed.
engineering_relevance: This enables safer coordination in multi-agent systems where only team-level constraint signals are available, improving credit assignment without sacrificing task performance.
method: Uses Signal Temporal Logic (STL) robustness to quantify episode-level constraint violation.
Computes smooth, differentiable full-episode robustness and action sensitivities from dynamics.
Allocates each running-maximum cost increment across agents at the same decision time, accounting for delayed effects.
evidence_signal: Across cooperative payload transport, connected navigation, and networked traffic control, SafeDiSTL outperformed constrained baselines with 1.6–5.1x higher safe-success in transport, 11.1% higher safe-success in navigation, and 50–68% more throughput in traffic.
watch_item: The approach depends on differentiable dynamics and accurate robustness gradients, which may limit direct use in highly non-smooth or poorly modeled environments.
paper_title: SafeDiSTL: Decomposing Joint Constraints for Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
